findings.finding: Root cause and fix independently verified by reading the diff directly (not trusting the implementer's summary). FullMap.tsx and MiniMap.tsx previously created their Leaflet map instance inside an async IIFE nested in useEffect; if unmount happened before `await import('leaflet')` resolved, the effect's synchronous cleanup ran as a no-op (nothing to remove yet), and the async callback later completed after unmount, attaching a full Leaflet instance (tiles, marker cluster, click listener, global `window.__mapListingClick`, ResizeObserver) with no registered cleanup — exactly the mechanism described in the Designer's analysis. The fix introduces a `cancelled` boolean captured at effect start, checked immediately after each await (and, defensively, right after `L.map()` construction), and the cleanup closure sets `cancelled = true` first before tearing down whatever was actually created. It also captures the container DOM node into a local `container` variable at effect start so cleanup/ResizeObserver logic no longer depends on `containerRef.current`, which React nulls during the same unmount commit — correctly fixing the second race the Designer flagged.
findings.evidence: rentals/frontend/src/components/map/FullMap.tsx lines 47-155; rentals/frontend/src/components/map/MiniMap.tsx lines 21-79 (git diff HEAD~1 reviewed directly).

Test file correctly documents what it cannot catch (real DOM/CSS pane leftovers, visual overlap, browser back/forward bfcache) matching the honesty required by the task.
